html:
The Northern Circars were a strip of coast on the Bay of Bengal, in today's Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha. On the 1800 map they are British territory.

The name comes from sarkar, a Mughal district. The five Circars belonged to the province of Golconda, later the Nizam's Dominions. In 1753 the Nizam gave them to the French, who paid for his troops. During the Carnatic Wars a British force took the French base at Masulipatam in 1759; see the siege of Masulipatam.

In 1765 the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the Circars to the East India Company, and a treaty with the Nizam confirmed it in 1766. They became part of the Madras Presidency. The Godavari and Krishna deltas, once the heart of Vengi, made the region rich in rice.
sum: The Northern Circars were a strip of coast on the Bay of Bengal, in today's Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha. On the 1800 map they are British territory.
